ai.title: Add background LLM conversation summarization for agent context
ai.summary: The agent runtime now generates structured conversation summaries in the background using the agent's own model to prepare for prompt cache expiration, replacing the previous mechanical history compaction. These summaries are stored on the agent state and applied via the `applyConversationSummary` utility when a user returns after a 5-minute idle gap or the context limit is reached. The SDK exposes a new `onCompactionSummary` callback and `withCompactionSummary` function, allowing the CLI to patch the saved run state with the finished summary to persist it across restarts, and the removal of `compactMechanically` eliminates the old synchronous path. Three additional Axiom telemetry events and new metadata correlation fields track the lifecycle, usage, and outcomes of these summary requests.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `common/src/constants/compaction-summary.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/conversation-summary.ts` which introduce the `ConversationSummary` type and background LLM summarization logic (`generateConversationSummary`), replacing the `compactMechanically` export removed from `packages/agent-runtime/src/compaction.ts` and the mechanical trigger logic in `run-agent-step.ts`.
ai.unknowns: The exact UI behavior for the user when a summary is generated or applied is not shown in the diff.

changes.what: Defines the instruction prompt, metadata constants, and the `ConversationSummary` type that track the context size and anchor of a structured summary.
Implements the background LLM summarization, idle return detection, and summary application, removing the old mechanical compaction export.
Adds allowlisted Axiom telemetry events and correlation fields to track the lifecycle, usage, and outcomes of compaction and summary requests.
Exposes `onCompactionSummary` in run options and provides `withCompactionSummary` to allow hosts to patch saved states with generated summaries.
Wires the `onCompactionSummary` callback into the CLI's run configuration and message sending to persist background summaries to the local chat state.

eli5.text: The AI assistant now writes a structured note of your conversation in the background while you are still working, so it has a fresh recap ready to use if you pause for more than five minutes or if the conversation gets too long to fit. When you come back, the assistant reads this note instead of the entire raw history, which helps it remember your requests without re-reading every detail. This is an internal efficiency update that does not change how you interact with the tool or affect your account limits; you will not see a new button or option, but the assistant may retain context better after breaks.

acceptedPr.title: ci: run the test suites, and fix what kept them red
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## Why

Green on this repo has never meant "the tests passed": `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installed dependencies, built the SDK, built the binary and smoke-tested it. No step ran `bun test` or `tsc`, so a red suite and a green check were indistinguishable — the second green check, `check`, is PR hygiene (title/body/forbidden paths).

That mattered while merging a batch of CLI PRs: reviewers were told the tests were green when no test had run, and running them showed **29 CLI failures and 11 SDK failures**, all pre-existing on `main`.

## What changes

**CI now runs the suites**, after the SDK build they need:

```yaml
- name: Typecheck
  run: |
    bun run --cwd=cli typecheck
    bun run --cwd=sdk typecheck
- name: Test
  run: |
    bun run --cwd=cli test
    bun run --cwd=sdk test
```

**And the suites now pass in the public export.** Each breakage fixed at its cause:

| failure | cause | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 22 suites failed to load | `cli/src/__tests__/test-utils.ts` threw when `packages/internal/src/env` was missing — and `packages/internal/` is on this mirror's forbidden-path list, so it is never here | fall back to the defaults it already installs; unchanged where the private module exists |
| `catalog mode sends the protocol header…` | the test read `fetch.mock.calls[0]` as the session POST, but device-key registration is now made first, so it read the wrong request | select the session calls by URL, and assert there are three |
| `fetchDockArm > returns control without an auth token` | "no token" was assumed; a machine with `~/.config/manicode/credentials.json` has one, so the fetch ran and returned `expandable` | pin `getAuthToken` to `undefined` for that test |
| 3 × `the mirrored in-place guidance` | reads `freebuff-desktop/src/server/services/sponsored-run.ts`, which this export withholds | `test.skipIf(!existsSync(...))`; the check is unchanged in the private tree |
| 2 × `SPONSORED_RUNTIME_PROBE_SCRIPT Python detection` | asserted the probe found *nothing at all*, which also carried the host's `node`/`npx` from `/usr/bin` | assert no `python`, which is what the test is about |

`tar` (required at load time by `cli/release-core/launcher.js`, and already declared by the published wrapper) and `@types/react-dom` join the root dev dependencies — the first is why three wrapper tests could not load, the second is why CLI typecheck reported 13 errors.

## Verification

```
bun run --cwd=cli test        → 4288 pass, 0 fail, 32 skip
bun run --cwd=sdk test        → 1070 pass, 0 fail, 16 skip
bun run --cwd=cli typecheck   → exit 0
bun run --cwd=sdk typecheck   → exit 0
```

Same commands on `main` before this change: 3940 pass / 29 fail and 1110 pass / 11 fail, with CLI typecheck 13 errors — the failure sets named above.

## What this does not do

It does not add coverage for the streaming/render path or for the compiled binary; the smoke step still only checks boot, the API URL and dotenv isolation. It makes the existing suites honest and run.

The cli/package.json test script sets NODE_ENV to test instead of production to align with test expectations. In common/src/types/json.ts, the JSONObject and JSONArray types are updated to use readonly modifiers to match how model SDKs type their payloads, resolving previous type errors in providerOptions assignments. A new Bun plugin in test/setup-scm-loader.ts is added to load .scm files as text exports for testing purposes.

acceptedPr.title: cli: report an injected preload at startup, and refuse on request
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## Why

A `--preload` / `-r` / `--require` module runs **before** any code the CLI ships. Nothing inside the binary can prevent that, so the binary should at least notice it and say so — once, in one line, without asking the user to configure anything.

## What changes

- `cli/src/utils/preload-guard.ts` (new): `foreignPreloadFrom({ execArgv, cwd, loadedModules })` returns the first preload outside the compiled bundle (`/$bunfs/`), or `null`. It understands `--preload x`, `--preload=x`, `-r x`, `--require=x`, exempts a repository `bunfig.toml` preload under the current directory, and treats the module cache as a best-effort second channel.
- `cli/src/index.tsx`: `main()` checks it first and prints one line if something was injected.

## No switches — for users or anyone else

The policy is `REFUSE_FOREIGN_PRELOAD`, a **constant in the module**, not an environment variable. There is nothing to set, nothing to unset, and no flag:

```
freebuff warning: code was injected into this process before it began (/path/to/hook.ts).
It has already run; the CLI continues.
```

Why a constant instead of a variable:

- A control that needs a variable is unset on every machine whose owner never read the release notes — the exact failure mode that makes guards decorative.
- A switch has to be documented to users, and this is not something a user should have to think about while launching a CLI.
- The preload has already executed by the time the check runs, so stopping cannot undo it; it can only take the CLI away from someone whose toolchain loads a module this way. The default therefore reports and continues, and a hardened distribution flips the constant in its own build.

The message asks for no variable, no flag, and never claims a refusal this build did not make — all three are pinned by tests.

## Limits, stated in the file

- The preload has already run when the check executes. This is a speed bump, not prevention.
- A `bunfig.toml` preload in the working directory is exempt by design (ordinary repository use).
- The module-cache channel is best-effort: a compiled binary may not expose CommonJS `require`.

## Verification

```text
cd cli && bun run typecheck                          → identical error set to the branch's baseline (13 pre-existing)
bun test src/utils/__tests__/preload-guard.test.ts   → 13 pass, 0 fail
```

13 tests: the three flag forms, a preload inside `/$bunfs/`, a cwd `bunfig` preload, the message wording, the absence of any user-facing switch, and the constant's own value.

## Note on the base

Sits on #1575 (the build fix) and #1577 (CI now runs the suites): `main` fails `Build SDK` on every commit, and until #1577 this repo's CI ran no tests. Rebased onto that pair so this PR's checks run `bun test` and `tsc` for real.

ai.title: Detect external process preloads at CLI startup and emit warning
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now detects external preloaded modules at startup to report process code injection. At launch in `main()` inside `cli/src/index.tsx`, the CLI calls `foreignPreloadFrom` from `cli/src/utils/preload-guard.ts` to inspect `process.execArgv` and module caches for paths outside the compiled bundle prefix `/$bunfs/` or current working directory. If an injected preload module is found via flags like `--preload`, `-r`, or `--require`, the CLI logs a warning via `describeForeignPreload` to notify the user. The guard policy uses the `REFUSE_FOREIGN_PRELOAD` constant, which defaults to `false` and allows execution to continue after logging.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/index.tsx, main() invokes foreignPreloadFrom and describeForeignPreload defined in cli/src/utils/preload-guard.ts to check process.execArgv and module caches for injected preloads.

eli5.text: The command-line assistant now checks at startup whether any outside code was loaded into the application before its own software started running. If an external file is detected, the terminal displays a brief warning message notifying you that outside code ran first. The tool continues operating as normal after showing the message, so your everyday experience remains unchanged unless your environment actively injects extra files.

entries.title: cli: scan only the seam for a completable think tag (#1573)

acceptedPr.title: cli: scan only the seam for a completable think tag
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## Why

Inside a text block, the streaming parser could only ever complete a `think` tag in two places: at the seam (the block's tail is a partial tag and the new delta finishes it) or wholly inside the new delta. The old code found those two cases by concatenating the block with the delta and searching the result — O(block) per chunk on any text that contains `<`, which is ordinary in code (`JSX`, XML, `a < b`). Over a stream that is quadratic.

## What changes

`appendTextWithThinkParsingToBlocks` checks the seam and the delta instead, and concatenates the block only when a tag is actually completable there:

- the seam probe reads at most `MAX_TAG_LENGTH_PLUS_ONE` characters from the block's tail, never the block;
- `text.includes('<think')` / `text.includes('</think')` on the delta is O(chunk);
- the full concatenation now happens only on the chunk that completes a tag.

Behaviour is unchanged: the tag split across chunk boundaries is still handled, and a tag that appears wholly inside a delta still splits the block.

## Performance

This branch, `bun` 1.4.2:

| fixture | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 470 KB code-heavy stream (`<` in every chunk), appended 200 chars at a time | concatenated the block per chunk — O(block), quadratic over the stream (the 470 KB case was measured at ~430 ms once blocks were long) | **6.51 ms** |

The old cost is not a constant either: it grew with the block, so the longer the answer, the more expensive each chunk became — which is the shape users see as the CLI slowing down late in a long reply.

## Verification

```text
cd cli && bun run typecheck                                  → identical error set to main
bun test src/utils/__tests__/block-operations-streaming.test.ts → 11 pass, 0 fail
```

`main` is red for an unrelated reason (`sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` provider options), so the typecheck line is a diff of the error output before and after, not an exit-0 claim.

The new tests stream a think tag split at **every** byte offset of `</think>` and ` thinking` and assert the same block shape as a single append, plus the case where the tag arrives whole inside a chunk.

## Risk

None found: the change is a scan restricted to the window where a tag can be completed, and the equivalence tests compare against the concatenating implementation's output at every split point. Rollback: revert the file.


## Base

Sits on #1575 (the build fix) and #1577 (CI now runs the suites). Rebased onto that pair, so this PR's checks run `bun test` and `tsc` for real instead of only building the tree and smoke-testing the binary.

ai.title: CLI think tag stream parser inspects block tail seam
ai.summary: In `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts`, `appendTextWithThinkParsingToBlocks` now inspects only the tail seam of existing text blocks when parsing think tags across chunk boundaries. Full string concatenation is deferred until a tag is completed at the seam or present in the incoming chunk, using `MAX_TAG_LENGTH_PLUS_ONE` to bound the search. This eliminates quadratic per-chunk string concatenation overhead when processing long streaming text containing `<` characters.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts`, `appendTextWithThinkParsingToBlocks` introduces `MAX_TAG_LENGTH_PLUS_ONE` to slice block tails and check tag seams before concatenating text blocks.

This internal improvement prevents the assistant from slowing down noticeably as a conversation grows long, keeping it responsive even when it is processing large amounts of text that contains common characters like angle brackets. You will not see a new feature or a change in what the assistant says; you will simply notice it keeps up more smoothly during long coding sessions. This is a maintenance update for the Freebuff engineering team and does not alter how the application behaves for you.

## Why

A fan-out spawns many `fast-worker` agents inside one message. An expanded worker draws every tool block it runs, so a wide fan-out is the one render path pagination does not bound: the page is capped by top-level message count, the agents nested inside one message are not.

Adds `'fast-worker'` to `COLLAPSED_BY_DEFAULT_AGENT_IDS`. `shouldCollapseByDefault` matches by substring, so `base3-fast-worker-deepseek-flash` and its per-model siblings all match. Collapsed, a worker still shows its last line and its children, so the result stays readable and one click expands the steps.

bun test src/utils/__tests__/block-processor.test.ts \

acceptedPr.title: cli: render streamed markdown incrementally instead of re-parsing the prefix
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## Why

A streamed answer was re-parsed from the top on every flush, so the cost of drawing one grew with the answer: at 200 KB a single flush spent ~46 ms parsing text that had already been rendered.

## What changes

`cli/src/utils/streaming-markdown.ts` (new) commits the document's *stable prefix* — the part no later delta can change — and parses only the newly committed slice. `markdown-renderer.tsx` grows the fence-aware contribution and hands it to the cache; four components (`single-block`, `agent-branch-wrapper`, `tool-branch`, `message-with-agents`) swap `ContentWithMarkdown` for the new `MarkdownBody`. `ContentWithMarkdown` stays in use by `user-content-copy.tsx`, so both paths remain live and tested.

Two pieces are one change because either alone is worthless:

- **Fence parity.** An unclosed code fence froze the cache: the prefix could not advance past it, so a long answer with a code block re-rendered from the top forever (measured: stuck at 13,859 of 200,000 characters). Whole fence lines are now sealed as literal text — an open fence only grows, so its complete lines cannot change — and the prefix keeps advancing.
- **The flat path parses only the new slice.** Re-rendering the whole prefix per commit is the same O(prefix) cost in a different place.

## Performance

200 KB fence-bearing fixture, 100 flushes, this branch, `bun` 1.4.2:

| path | total | per flush |
|---|---|---|
| full parse | 4,601.4 ms | 46.01 ms |
| cached | 247.3 ms | 2.47 ms |

**18.6×**, and flat in the length of the answer instead of growing with it.

## Correctness

Rendering is unchanged, and the test asserts it rather than asserting a speed: `streaming-markdown.test.tsx` compares full-parse output against cached output frame by frame at every line boundary of the fixture (13 tests), and two further tests pin the parity invariant itself — the cache's committed prefix advances monotonically and ends within one block of the content — which is the assertion that would have caught the fence freeze.

```text
cd cli && bun run typecheck                                → identical error set to main
bun test src/utils/__tests__/streaming-markdown.test.tsx \
         src/components/__tests__/message-with-agents.test.tsx → 35 pass, 0 fail
```

`main` is red for an unrelated reason (`sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` provider options, 23 errors in `cli` across the `sdk` import graph), so the typecheck line above is a diff of the error output before and after this branch, not an exit-0 claim.

## Risk

- Layout: five call sites move from one `<text>` to a `<box>` of many `<text>` chunks. The equivalence tests cover the message paths; the agent body nested inside a `Button` is not framed by any test, so a visual check of one long agent answer is worth doing.
- Cache invalidation is by palette identity: a caller that builds `{...palette}` inline turns the incremental path off (output stays correct, the speedup disappears). Every current caller memoizes the palette.
- Rollback: revert the commit; the components return to `ContentWithMarkdown`.


## Base

Sits on #1575 (the build fix) and #1577 (CI now runs the suites). Rebased onto that pair, so this PR's checks run `bun test` and `tsc` for real instead of only building the tree and smoke-testing the binary.

ai.title: CLI renders streamed markdown incrementally instead of re-parsing
ai.summary: The CLI now renders streaming markdown incrementally by committing the document's stable prefix and parsing only newly appended slices, rather than re-parsing the entire answer from the top on every flush. The new `MarkdownBody` component in `cli/src/components/blocks/markdown-body.tsx` chunks rendered blocks into `MARKDOWN_CHUNK_CHARS` (2000) character segments, and four components (`single-block.tsx`, `agent-branch-wrapper.tsx`, `tool-branch.tsx`, and `message-with-agents.tsx`) now use this component instead of `ContentWithMarkdown`. This change also includes a fence-parity fix where complete lines of an open code fence are sealed as literal text to allow the cache prefix to advance past it, reducing per-flush parsing time from ~46 ms to 2.47 ms for a 200 KB document.
ai.evidence: New files `cli/src/utils/streaming-markdown.ts` (introducing `StreamingMarkdownCache` and `renderStreamingMarkdownGroups`) and `cli/src/components/blocks/markdown-body.tsx` (exporting `MarkdownBody`), with four CLI components (`agent-branch-wrapper.tsx`, `single-block.tsx`, `tool-branch.tsx`, `message-with-agents.tsx`) swapping `ContentWithMarkdown` for `MarkdownBody`.

eli5.text: The Freebuff terminal assistant now shows streaming answers faster by remembering which parts of the text are already finished and only redrawing the newest section, instead of re-reading the entire message every time a new chunk arrives. This makes long AI responses appear more smoothly without freezing the interface. You will notice the chat scroll and update more fluidly as the assistant types out answers, with no changes to your settings or account required.

acceptedPr.title: cli: append streamed root text once per flush, not once per delta
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## Why

The batched message updater applies its queue once per 100 ms, but that batching was only half done: every streamed `text`/`reasoning` delta was queued as its own closure, so a flush called `appendTextToRootStream` once per token. That function starts with `const nextBlocks = [...blocks]` — a shallow copy of every block in the message — so a long answer copied the whole block array per token.

## What changes

- `PendingUpdate` becomes a tagged union: `{ kind: 'updater' }` for existing queued closures, `{ kind: 'rootText', delta }` for streamed text.
- `appendRootText` merges a delta into the tail entry when both are `rootText` of the same type, so consecutive deltas collapse into one string per window. An interleaved non-text update ends the merge, so ordering is preserved by construction.
- `flush` composes the queue into a single transform and applies it in one `setMessages`, appending text once per text type per window.
- `appendRootChunk` (`utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts`) calls `updater.appendRootText(delta)` instead of wrapping `appendTextToRootStream` in a closure.

No primitive, component or render path changes.

## Performance

`bun` 1.4.2, same machine:

| fixture | per-delta (before) | after |
|---|---|---|
| 200 KB answer, 26,572 deltas | 765.2 ms | 19.7 ms at 100 deltas/flush — 39× (22.5 ms at 50, 41.8 ms at 25) |
| 2,040,000 chars, 291,429 deltas, 20,001 blocks | 23,949.6 ms | 352.6 ms at 200 deltas/flush |

The second row is the case that produced a multi-second stall late in a long, tag-heavy reply: the cost was the per-token block-array copy, and at the shipped cadence the product no longer pays it.

## Verification

```text
cd cli && bun run typecheck                          → identical error set to main
bun test src/utils/__tests__/message-updater.test.ts → 27 pass, 0 fail
```

`main` is red for an unrelated reason (`sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` provider options, 23 errors in `cli`), so the typecheck line is a diff of the error output before and after this branch, not an exit-0 claim.

New tests:

- **`merged deltas produce the same blocks as one append each`** — the same delta sequence through the batched updater and, one at a time, through `appendTextToRootStream`; the block shapes (content, `textType`, `thinkingOpen`) must be equal.
- **`a flush boundary and an interleaved update keep arrival order`** — text, flush, more text, an interleaved block update, flush: the text must read `before after|tool output`.

## Risk and rollback

- Text now reaches the screen up to one flush window (≤100 ms) later — the window the updater already had for every other update.
- Merging only touches adjacent entries of the same type; any interleaved update ends the merge.
- One place output can differ, and it is pre-existing: at a delta boundary that cuts a `think` tag the parser already mis-splits, and merging removes split points rather than adding them. On an adversarial 7-char-split fixture the coalesced path preserved 5,405–5,546 of 5,640 text characters where per-delta feeding preserved 47. Fixing the primitive is a separate change (#1573 is the same area).
- Rollback: revert the two source files; behaviour returns to one append per delta.


## Base

Sits on #1575 (the build fix) and #1577 (CI now runs the suites). Rebased onto that pair, so this PR's checks run `bun test` and `tsc` for real instead of only building the tree and smoke-testing the binary.

ai.title: Batch streamed root text deltas to reduce block array copies
ai.summary: The CLI batched message updater now merges consecutive streamed text and reasoning deltas into a single string per flush window instead of queuing each delta as a separate closure. This change replaces the previous mechanism that called `appendTextToRootStream` once per token, which repeatedly copied the entire block array. The `appendRootChunk` function in `sdk-event-handlers.ts` is updated to use the new `appendRootText` method to pass structured deltas directly to the updater.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/message-updater.ts`, `PendingUpdate` is changed from a closure array to a tagged union and `appendRootText` merges consecutive `rootText` deltas of the same type; in `cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts`, `appendRootChunk` now calls `updater.appendRootText(delta)` instead of wrapping `appendTextToRootStream` in a closure.

eli5.text: The text-display system in the terminal app now combines short text updates that arrive within the same hundred-thousandth-of-a-second window into a single, larger update instead of copying the entire message repeatedly for each tiny fragment. This internal efficiency improvement makes the terminal app more responsive when displaying long AI replies. You will not notice a difference in what the assistant says or how it behaves, but the app may feel slightly smoother when processing large outputs.

acceptedPr.title: cli: scale the checkpoint interval with the transcript
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## Why

In-flight state checkpoints were written on a fixed 5 s cadence no matter how large the chat had grown, so the largest transcripts paid the most expensive setting: a checkpoint is two multi-MB serializations and two fsyncs, and it ran every five seconds until the run ended.

## What changes

`utils/run-state-storage.ts` gains the interval rule and a single reader for it:

| persisted state | interval |
|---|---|
| < 8 MB | 5 s |
| 8 – < 16 MB | 10 s |
| 16 – < 24 MB | 15 s |
| ≥ 24 MB | 20 s |

`checkpointIntervalMsForStateBytes` is the pure rule (5 s base, +5 s per 8 MB, capped at 20 s); `checkpointIntervalMsForChat` stats the chat's `run-state.json` and `chat-messages.json` once per run and applies it. `use-send-message.ts` passes the result to the SDK as `stateSnapshotIntervalMs`, and `create-run-config` forwards it.

**Based on #1571** (`sdk/state-snapshot-interval`): the option is the SDK's. Without that PR this change is inert — the field would be dropped and the interval would stay 5 s.

## Cost that must be stated

A crash can now lose up to **20 s** of run state instead of 5 s, and 20 s is first reached at 24 MB of persisted state, not at 12 MB. Below 8 MB nothing changes.

## Verification

```text
cd cli && bun run typecheck                            → identical error set to main
bun test src/__tests__/unit/create-run-config.test.ts  → 44 pass, 0 fail
```

`main` is red for an unrelated reason (`sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` provider options), so the typecheck line is a diff of the error output before and after, not an exit-0 claim.

The new tests cover the boundaries of the table (0, just under 8 MB, exactly 8 MB, 24 MB and above), that a missing chat directory falls back to the base interval, and that the value reaches the run config.

## Risk and rollback

Only the checkpoint cadence changes; every write is still atomic and still happens on completion. Rollback: revert the commit and the SDK falls back to its own default.


## Base

Sits on #1575 (the build fix) and #1577 (CI now runs the suites). Rebased onto that pair, so this PR's checks run `bun test` and `tsc` for real instead of only building the tree and smoke-testing the binary.

ai.title: Scale CLI state checkpoint interval with transcript size
ai.summary: The CLI now scales state checkpoint intervals based on persisted transcript file size rather than persisting every 5 seconds. Transcripts under 8 MB retain the default 5-second interval, while larger sessions scale up to 20 seconds at 24 MB or more to reduce CPU stalls from frequent serialization and fsync operations. `checkpointIntervalMsForChat` in `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` stats chat files once per run and passes `stateSnapshotIntervalMs` to `run` in `sdk/src/run.ts`.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts, checkpointIntervalMsForChat stats chat files to calculate state checkpoint intervals, which cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts passes to the SDK via stateSnapshotIntervalMs in sdk/src/run.ts.

changes.what: Scale the in-flight run state checkpoint save interval based on disk transcript file sizes.
Add stateSnapshotIntervalMs run option and snapshotSessionState helper for shallow state snapshotting.

eli5.text: The Freebuff assistant now saves its progress report less often when your chat history is very long, instead of always saving every five seconds. This change is aimed at people using the Freebuff command-line tool or developer SDK who are running extended coding sessions. In daily use, you will notice fewer brief pauses or stutters in the terminal while the assistant is working, because the program no longer spends as much time repeatedly writing the entire large conversation to your hard drive.
